items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, its cheapest and fastest small model yet
items.summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on October 7, calling it its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model to date. Pricing is $0.10/$0.50 per million input tokens and as low as $0.50 per million output tokens for prompts up to 100k tokens, which Anthropic says cuts costs about 75% versus Haiku 4.5 on average (up to 90% for shorter prompts). It's also the first Haiku-class model with an adjustable reasoning-effort setting (Low through Max), and ships now on the Anthropic API, AWS, and Google Cloud.
items.whyItMatters: A small model this cheap and fast, with tunable effort, is a strong fit for the high-volume backend work around Romain and Anna — grading, summarizing transcripts, classification — without paying Sonnet or Opus rates.

items.title: Mistral AI previews Large 4 ("Le Chonk"), a 1.05T-parameter open-weight MoE model
items.summary: Mistral opened a public preview of Large 4 on October 6 via its moderated API: a mixture-of-experts model with roughly 1.05 trillion total parameters (about 49B active), a 1.6B-parameter vision encoder for multimodal input, and training data spanning 160+ languages. Open weights are planned for release by the end of October, pending ongoing safety testing with outside researchers.
items.whyItMatters: A new large multilingual model from a French lab, with open weights coming, is worth benchmarking for any backend LLM task behind Romain or Anna that needs strong French-language handling at a lower cost than closed frontier APIs.

items.title: ElevenLabs targets a 2028 IPO as its voice agents cross 15M weekly conversations
items.summary: Reports on October 6-7 say ElevenLabs is preparing for a 2028 IPO after a $300M employee tender offer valued the company at $22B, double its February valuation. ElevenLabs says its AI voice agents now handle more than 15 million conversations a week, roughly triple the February figure, with banks and insurers increasingly deploying them for customer service.
items.whyItMatters: That kind of enterprise voice-agent growth usually comes with fast-moving API changes and new pricing tiers — worth tracking for anything that could affect Anna's ElevenLabs integration.

items.title: Anthropic restructures its Cyber Verification Program into three access tiers
items.summary: On October 6, Anthropic reorganized its Cyber Verification Program into Defense Access, Red Team Access, and Specialized Access tiers, merging in the earlier Project Glasswing critical-infrastructure program. All tiers cover Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1, loosening cyber-related blocking classifiers for vetted security professionals doing legitimate dual-use work.
items.whyItMatters: Not voice-specific, but a useful reference for how Anthropic scopes access and safety classifiers for sensitive-but-legitimate use cases, in case Romain or Anna's stack ever needs something similar.
